text: Three seconds of rage left. The clapper slams onto two raised shields, Lyra crouched on the rim at full draw.
Pass: Jaeha routes the blow's force from Borro through his own body toward Lyra, and lights up like a wire.
Then his knees buckle, his hand slips off her heel, and the light scatters into sparks.
Blood gushes from his nose. Seventy percent of the force spills into the water.
Lyra fires anyway, with only a flicker of light on the arrow.
It sinks halfway into the crack and sticks. The crack widens, but the bronze holds.
Lyra is livid. Her big debut, and her shot is wedged in the bronze like a splinter.
And the rage clock hits zero.
The giant throws its arms wide, and its bell-head swings by itself, like a bell in a tower.
The great toll. Half the dome blows out, every hanging bell shatters, and Borro's shield holds over them all.
Dust and water rain through new shafts of daylight. The giant sways, the arrow still in its bell.
Jaeha lies in the water, bleeding from his nose and ear. He tries to get up. His legs don't answer.
Yerin crawls to him, shouting his name. He can't hear a thing.
She presses her glowing hands over his ears.
The ringing fades, and his eyes find her. His hearing is back. His legs aren't.
Through the dust, the giant turns toward them, ash pouring from the widened crack.
Lyra notches another arrow, counting her quiver now, and losing patience with the merchant.
He does: a shaky line from shield to stick figure to bow. He circles the figure's legs. The plan was fine. His legs weren't.
So he turns to the one man here he has no reason to trust, and asks to be held up.
Jaeha's eyes don't waver. Mok let go of him once, at Gate 0912, and they both know it.
That lands like a blow. Mok looks away.
Then the tank lets his own shield fall into the water.
Nib's cooldown ends, and the amber flares back: five more minutes of field form, the only form he can fight in.
Jaeha splits the job: Nib drops the giant to shield height, Lyra holds her shot. This time, his legs are Mok's problem.
Nib races through the rubble, stone to stone.
He hacks at the back of the giant's knee, again and again.
The giant crashes onto one knee, its bell-head level with the shields, and raises the clapper.
Behind Jaeha, Mok grips his shoulders and holds him upright. He says it twice, as if to convince himself.
Jaeha's fingertips touch Lyra's heel. A faint glow starts.
Point-blank, Lyra whispers her boast again. This time she'd very much like it to be true.
The clapper comes down.
It slams onto Borro's shield, and Borro does not move an inch.
Borrowed Thunder. The blow's force runs in one blinding chain: through Borro, through Jaeha in Mok's hands, through Lyra, into the arrow.
She lets go, and the arrow leaves with the ring of the giant's own bell.
It punches straight through the bell-head, and the bell splits from top to bottom.
The giant crumbles into violet ash from the top down.
Ash falls like snow in the daylight. Nobody moves.
Then Jaeha sags in Mok's hands, laughing breathlessly.
A violet core rises from the empty robes. Boss defeated, B-grade. The gate closes in ten minutes.
And a new combo: Borrowed Thunder. Borro, through the Operator, to Lyra.
Lyra hops down and walks straight past the wounded to the drone in Borro's moss. Priorities.
A wink and a peace sign for the lens, then straight to business: the merchant owes her.
Then a third window, with one button: harvest the core, nine hundred million won. No other option. Nib looks away.
Yerin stares, hands over her mouth. Jaeha sees his sister's future in that number, then looks at Nib. Five on his list now, and never a release.
Lyra and Nib haul the last stones off Borro, and he finally rises from the rubble.
Outside, the stream passes one point one million, and the chat is crying over Mok, of all people.
Jaeha presses Harvest, and the core drifts into his hands.
Level six, and the new kind of boss refills the meter toward his next call, from zero to sixty percent.
Mok sinks onto a broken bell, staring at the hands that held Jaeha up. He has no idea what he just did.
Jaeha sits down beside him, the core in his lap. His answer: a job title, and a bolted door.
Mok can't meet his eyes.
Lyra looks Mok over, curious. One fight together, and she's already read him.
Nib introduces him in three flat words.
The notebook falls open at the page he wrote the night Choi showed him the report.
Then, very quietly, Jaeha says Minseok's name to the man who signed his death off as an accident.
Mok's eyes go flat and dead, the way they were at the start.
Then his radio crackles: six of his hunters are through the crypt, waiting at the end of Jaeha's way out.
Mok stands slowly and lifts his cracked shield from the water, his face in shadow.
Nine minutes twelve until the gate closes.
High on the back wall, in a doorway six metres up, a slender silhouette steps out with a crossbow.
Han Sora, smiling down at them, her brass compass on her wrist.
Her needle, which hunts summons, swings to Lyra, then on to Jaeha and the core in his lap.
She congratulates the hero sweetly, then asks the only question left: nine hundred million won, and who walks out holding it?
Jaeha's arms tighten around the core. The boss is dead. The danger isn't.
